newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends broadly lower on harvest outlook.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends broadly lower on harvest outlook.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled broadly lower amid record-setting volume as weather conditions looked set to allow harvest to advance this weekend in the central U.S. Plains, traders said.
Showers this week slowed combining of the Kansas crop, but meteorologists said Friday they expected favorable weather for the harvest through Sunday.

Traders said harvest pressure built throughout the day. Further weakness came when Chicago July wheat set a new contract low at $3.25 per bushel, breaking the contract's previous lifetime low of $3.28.
Friday's KCBT HRW wheat futures volume was estimated at 91.255 million bushels, well above the previous single-day record of 81.355 million bushels.
Traders said the July/Sept carry narrowed throughout the session on bull-spreading tied to speculative short positions being rolled into deferred months.
General Mills bought July late, helping to narrow the July/Sept spread. The spread traded between seven and eight cents most of the session and closed on paper at 5-1/4 cents.
Overall, KCBT wheat settled six to 9-1/2 cents lower, with July down six cents at $3.39-1/4.
Traders said they had noted some scale-down commercial buying on the session, with Cargill Investor Services picking up 2.8 million Sept and 1.7 million July.
